commits.message:
chore(ci): debuggable status assertion + engine-anchored node version

Two findings from the Copilot re-review:

1. `#status.ok` composite selector hid boot-error text. On crash,
   mount.ts.tmpl sets `class="err"` with a "boot error: ..." message;
   waiting on the composite selector reduced the failure output to
   "selector timeout" instead of the real error. Locate `#status` by id
   only, then assert class and text separately so Playwright prints the
   actual received class and current text on failure. The triple-assert
   semantics are unchanged; only the failure surface improves.
   [LAW:verifiable-goals]

2. `node-version: 20` could in principle resolve to a 20.x older than
   the `engines.node` constraint (`^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`, set by a
   transitive dep). Use `node-version-file: package.json` so setup-node
   consults the canonical engine declaration — the workflow cannot
   drift from the package.json constraint, and an engine bump
   propagates to CI automatically. [LAW:one-source-of-truth]

All 7 demos still pass; `npm run lint` clean.

chore(ci): assert .xterm-rows textContent, not .xterm-screen child count

xterm.js populates .xterm-screen's layer children (helpers, style,
.xterm-rows, .xterm-selection, .xterm-decoration-container — six in total)
during term.open(), *before* any write. Asserting `screen.children.length
> 0` therefore proves only that xterm initialised, not that the demo
produced output — a demo that crashed silently between term.open() and
its first write() would have passed the previous check.

The correct demo-wrote-data signal is `.xterm-rows` textContent: 30 row
divs are present unconditionally, but their textContent is whitespace
until something writes. `expect(rows).toContainText(/\S/)` polls until at
least one non-whitespace character appears — the failure mode the gate
was designed to catch.

Verified by probing the live DOM: .xterm-rows.textContent on rich-strip
contained the rendered banner ("main | claude.ai | 3.4k tok | 12%
...") with 1326 chars across 30 rows; all 7 demos still pass.
[LAW:verifiable-goals]

chore(ci): headless-browser gate for live demo pages (rich-demo-site-pek.5)

Playwright smokes every demo in `docs/.vitepress/demos.json` against the
real built docs output (`vitepress preview docs`). For each manifest entry
the test asserts the triple pattern that catches every demo-boot failure
mode independently: `#status.ok` contains "ready" (mount shell completed),
`.xterm-screen` is attached with rendered rows (xterm initialised AND
demo wrote data), and zero console errors / uncaught exceptions (no silent
throws on the boot path). [LAW:verifiable-goals]

The demo list lives in the manifest — adding or removing a demo updates
CI coverage with no test edits. [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow]
[LAW:one-source-of-truth]

CI gains `npm run docs:build` → `playwright install --with-deps chromium`
→ `npm run test:demos`, with the HTML report uploaded as an artefact only
on failure. A minimal `vitest.config.ts` scopes vitest to `test/` so the
two runners don't fight over `*.spec.ts`. [LAW:locality-or-seam]

feat(docs): live demos on docs site (rich-demo-site-pek.4) (#44)

* feat(docs): VitePress Demos section with live xterm.js terminals (rich-demo-site-pek.4)

Surface every browser-bundled demo as a runnable page inside the existing
docs site. One pipeline (npm run docs:build), one deploy (docs.yml +
gh-pages-multiplexer), one source of truth for the demo list (the manifest
the bundle pipeline writes).

- vite.config.demos.ts: output to docs/public/demos-app/ so VitePress's
  public-files convention copies bundles to dist/demos-app/ verbatim; also
  emit docs/.vitepress/demos.json (the canonical demo list).
- docs/demos/[demo].md + [demo].paths.ts: VitePress dynamic-route page
  that iframes /demos-app/<name>/, with paths derived from the manifest.
- docs/demos/index.md: landing page listing all demos from the same
  manifest — adding/removing a demo updates the index automatically.
- docs/.vitepress/config.ts: read manifest at config-load, add Demos nav
  + sidebar section. No second list to maintain.
- package.json: docs:build / docs:dev chain demos:build first; demos.json
  is a precondition, not a fallback. Missing manifest fails loud.
- .gitignore: docs/public/demos-app/ + docs/.vitepress/demos.json are
  build artifacts; dist-demos/ is retired.

Verified via Chrome MCP against docs:preview: index lists 7 demos with
correct /rich-js/ base; rich-strip + themes-and-color-studio both load
status="ready", xterm-screen rendered with content, zero console errors.
8881/8881 vitest pass.

* chore(lint): extend tsc --noEmit to docs/ TypeScript files

docs/.vitepress/config.ts and docs/demos/*.ts were authoring TypeScript
files that no lint command touched — neither the main `tsc --noEmit`
(which scopes to src/) nor tsconfig.scripts.json (which only included
vite.config.demos.ts). Pulling them into tsconfig.scripts.json puts
every TS file in the repo under exactly one type-check gate.
[LAW:single-enforcer] [LAW:verifiable-goals]

Surfaced a pre-existing latent bug in config.ts: `process.env.VITEPRESS_BASE`
violated noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature. Fixed in place.

fix(coverage): label every allowlist entry by its actual export kind

Copilot review on PR #35 flagged that the reason string for KeyEvent
called it a "type" when src/widgets/types.ts declares it as a class.
A reader debugging a coverage failure consumes that reason string
verbatim — a wrong label is misleading guidance, not just imprecision.

The same pattern was repeated across many entries (I had labeled most
interfaces as "type" and several classes as "type"). Rather than
fix only the entry Copilot named, a derivation pass over src/ rewrote
every reason string from the actual export declaration:

  - class      → "<scope>: <Name> class"
  - interface  → "<scope>: <Name> interface"
  - type       → "<scope>: <Name> type alias"
  - const      → "<scope>: <Name> constant"
  - function   → "<scope>: <Name> function"
  - enum       → "<scope>: <Name> enum"

83 lines of labels updated. Existing parenthetical context (e.g.
"used transitively via Pretty") is preserved.

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] The src/ declaration is the canonical
description of an export's kind. A reason string that disagrees with
it is a divergent copy — fix the divergence by deriving from the
source, not by patching the copy point-by-point.

Verification: npm run lint clean; coverage verifier still green
(4/4).

chore(demos): retire flagship-per-domain spec and typing

Removes the artifacts that encoded the over-fit "exactly five flagships
with strict source-module ownership" model the previous demo-tune-up
design produced. The lit epic (rich-demos-l2x) has already been
rewritten back to the user's original ask (dedupe / expand / consolidate
/ reorganize / tweak — fewer + more interesting demos, with existing
working demos preserved until something better replaces them).

# Changes

- **Deleted `spec/demos.md`** — the 392-line spec that defined five
  flagships with rigid source-module ownership and mandated deleting the
  interactive TUIs (rich-explore, claude-sessions) to satisfy the count.
  Retired in favor of judgment-driven concrete improvements.

- **`test/coverage/coverage-allowlist.ts`** — dropped the `Flagship`
  string-literal union, the `burndown(flagship)` helper, and the
  discriminated-union `AllowlistEntry` (`{ kind: "burndown" }`
  vs `{ kind: "permanent" }`). Collapsed to one flat shape:
  `AllowlistEntry { reason: string }`. Per-flagship comment headers
  replaced with factual "-- from src/X --" sectioning. [LAW:absorbed-variance]
  — the discriminated union only had one realized case (burndown);
  collapse to one shape.

- **`test/coverage/coverage.test.ts`** — softened the file header
  comment (no longer claims to be "the keystone" of an epic; explicitly
  notes the verifier is a *floor*, not a quality measure). Updated the
  error messages and the redundant-entry detail to match the new
  AllowlistEntry shape.

- **`examples/themes-and-color-studio/index.ts`** — header comment no
  longer calls the demo "the flagship"; describes what it actually is
  (a printed-tour reference kept for the color subsystem, not a template
  for future demos). One-liner inside main() and one in-line infra
  comment updated to match.

# Verification

- npm run lint: clean
- npx vitest run: 8838 passed | 7 skipped (328 files)
- npm run themes-and-color-studio: runs to completion

# What is NOT changed

No demos under `examples/` are deleted. All existing demos
(`rich-explore`, `claude-sessions`, `rich-themes`, `rich-themes-transposed`,
`rich-theme-designer`, `rich-colors`, `rich-config`, `dropdown-demo`,
`rich-dash`, `rich-markup-plugins`, `rich-strip`, `rich-template-bindings`,
`themes-and-color-studio`, `shared`) remain on disk; their npm scripts
remain wired. Per parent epic non-goal: working demos are not deleted
before something concrete has replaced them and been judged a
replacement.
